questions.stem: Which of the following is not true regarding the adverse effect profile of colchicine:

options.label: A
options.text: Nausea, diarrhoea is dose-independent adverse effects

options.label: B
options.text: Overdose can produce renal failure, CNS depression

options.label: C
options.text: Death in overdose may occur due to muscle paralysis and respiratory failure

options.label: D
options.text: If given for prophylaxis or chronic gout, agranulocytosis may occur

questions.answerText: Nausea, diarrhoea is dose-independent adverse effects
questions.solutionHtml:
Nausea, diarrhoea is dose-independent adverse effects
  • Reason- Nausea, vomiting, and diarrhoea are dose-limiting adverse effects


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 232

questions.solutionHtml:

questions.solutionHtml:

questions.stem: A patient was started on Allopurinol therapy for chronic gout. He developed a pruritic maculopapular rash. What is the next step?

options.label: B
options.text: continue Allopurinol, as the rash will subside gradually

questions.solutionHtml:
Discontinue allopurinol
  • Gout happens when there’s too much uric acid in your body and it forms crystals which can appear around your joints and kidneys and cause pain. This medicine helps to keep uric acid levels low.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 234

questions.stem: Allopurinol is useful in all of the following diseases except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Dermatitis herpetiformis
  • Dermatitis herpetiformis(DH) is a chronic autoimmune blistering skin condition, characterised by intensely itchy blisters filled with a watery fluid. DH is a cutaneous manifestation of coeliac disease, although the exact causal mechanism is not known. DH is neither related to nor caused by the herpes virus;

questions.stem: Among the following options, what is the mechanism of action of Colchicine?
questions.solutionHtml:
Microtubular protein depolymerization
  • Colchicine binds to tubulin, a microtubular protein, causing its de-polymerisation.
  • This disrupts cellular functions, such as the mobility of granulocytes, thus decreasing their migration into the affected area.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 231

questions.stem: Which drug among the following options acts through decreased neutrophil recruitment?
questions.solutionHtml:
Colchicine
  • Colchicine works by decreasing swelling and lessening the build-up of uric acid crystals that cause pain in the affected joint (s). This medication is also used to prevent attacks of pain in the abdomen, chest, or joints caused by a certain inherited disease (familial Mediterranean fever).


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 231, 232
